title: On-call decision trees, smart throttling, and coordinated failover playflows
creator: Priya Natarajan
description:
Problem: We continue to receive high-volume P0/P1 paging noise during transient regional overloads. Current alerts fire on raw error rates and queue depth, producing duplicate pages across regions and unnecessary escalations. Existing runbooks are free-text and require on-call judgment, causing slow mitigation and inconsistent failovers.

Goal: Deliver a deterministic on-call decision-tree (playflow) that pairs compact alert signals with automated short-circuit mitigations: coordinated circuit-breaker tripping, regional traffic shedding, and a delayed cross-region failover. Automate the low-risk steps so humans only intervene for escalations. Reduce page volume by 60% for non-actionable events and cut mean time to mitigation (MTTM) for region overloads by 50%.

Scope: Alert rule tuning and tagging, a formal decision-tree document for on-call, automation hooks (server-side throttles and job to flip circuit breakers), dashboard panels for attribution, and a small library of production-safe scripts for automated mitigations. Work includes integrations with PagerDuty, Opsgenie (if present), Console routing controls, and Grafana.

Non-goals: Full self-healing across every failure mode. This ticket focuses on overload and degraded latency events that are predictable by our request/queue/kv-cache signals, not data corruption or security incidents.
acceptance_criteria: Compact decision-tree doc published in Confluence with explicit thresholds and escalation steps
Alert rules adjusted so alerts include attributed region, model, and lane (streaming vs batch) labels
Automated throttle endpoint that applies short-lived (30s-2m) token-based shedding implemented and tested in staging
Circuit-breaker orchestration script that can be invoked by automation and by on-call with a single button in Console
Pager volume reduction: non-actionable pages for regional overloads reduced by >= 60% in first-week rollout metrics
Failover ramp: when automation trips a local circuit, traffic spillover to healthy region completes within SLO thresholds in 90% of simulated events
Playflow run in a full scale chaos simulation with postmortem and runbook updates

mitigation_steps: Immediate: Silence noisy non-actionable alerts (temporarily) and enable composite region-overload alert with 60s suppression
If composite alert fires: automated throttle endpoint invocation (apply 30s token-based shedding) and tag event with 'auto-throttle'
If errors persist > 90s after throttle: orchestrator flips local circuit-breaker to degraded mode (rejects low-priority lanes) and triggers cross-region spillover policy
Manual override: Console button labeled 'Force local CB' with an optional note; triggers rollback of automated measures when safe
Post-incident: Run the checklist in playflow doc and attach logs (request traces + KV cache metrics) to the incident ticket
rollout_notes: Stage A (on-call group A): enable compact alerts and automation in non-prod and a single prod region for 48h
Stage B: expand to two pilot regions and keep manual override readily available for SRE
Stage C: global rollout if pilot metrics meet thresholds (>=60% page reduction and MTTM improvement)
Rollback criteria: increased customer errors outside simulated windows or automation-caused cascading rejects
